concepts.def: Net movement of particles from a high to a low concentration; passive.
Diffusion of water across a partially permeable membrane.
Movement of substances against a concentration gradient, requiring energy.
The difference in concentration that drives diffusion.
Lets some molecules (e.g. water) through but not others.
A larger ratio speeds exchange; large organisms need transport systems.

walkthroughs.body_html:
Movement Into & Out of Cells — a core area of GCSE Biology.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Movement Into & Out of Cells brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Movement Into & Out of Cells.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: Which of these is a prokaryote?
options: Human skin cell
Yeast
Bacterium
Onion cell
protein synthesis
photosynthesis
aerobic respiration
cell division

mcqs.q: What is the key structural difference between prokaryotic and eukaryotic cells?
options: Prokaryotes have no DNA — that's why they have no nucleus.
Mitochondria store sunlight and release it for photosynthesis.
Prokaryotes are always smaller than 1 micrometre and have no cytoplasm.
Eukaryotes have a membrane-bound nucleus and membrane-bound organelles; prokaryotes do not.

mcqs.q: What is the main role of mitochondria in a cell?
options: Mitochondria store sunlight and release it for photosynthesis.
Mitosis happens in plants and meiosis happens in animals.
To carry out aerobic respiration, producing ATP that cells use as an energy currency.
Mitochondria produce energy by creating it from nothing.

mcqs.q: What is the key difference between mitosis and meiosis?
options: Mitosis happens in plants and meiosis happens in animals.
Mitosis produces two genetically identical diploid cells; meiosis produces four genetically different haploid cells (gametes).
Prokaryotes are always smaller than 1 micrometre and have no cytoplasm.
Mitosis and meiosis both produce gametes; they are basically the same.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Subcellular structures”?
options: The smallest unit of life; carries out the functions needed to live.
Parts inside a cell with specific jobs: nucleus, mitochondria, ribosomes, chloroplasts.
Cells adapted for a specific role, e.g. red blood cell, sperm, root hair.
Undifferentiated cell that can divide to form many cell types.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Stem cell”?
options: A cell with a nucleus enclosed in a membrane; e.g. animal, plant, fungus cells.
The smallest unit of life; carries out the functions needed to live.
Undifferentiated cell that can divide to form many cell types.
Cells adapted for a specific role, e.g. red blood cell, sperm, root hair.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Cell”?
options: A smaller cell with no nucleus; DNA is a loop in the cytoplasm; e.g. bacteria.
Undifferentiated cell that can divide to form many cell types.
Cells adapted for a specific role, e.g. red blood cell, sperm, root hair.
The smallest unit of life; carries out the functions needed to live.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Eukaryotic cell”?
options: A smaller cell with no nucleus; DNA is a loop in the cytoplasm; e.g. bacteria.
Cells adapted for a specific role, e.g. red blood cell, sperm, root hair.
A cell with a nucleus enclosed in a membrane; e.g. animal, plant, fungus cells.
Undifferentiated cell that can divide to form many cell types.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Prokaryotic cell”?
options: A smaller cell with no nucleus; DNA is a loop in the cytoplasm; e.g. bacteria.
Undifferentiated cell that can divide to form many cell types.
Parts inside a cell with specific jobs: nucleus, mitochondria, ribosomes, chloroplasts.
Cells adapted for a specific role, e.g. red blood cell, sperm, root hair.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Specialised cells”?
options: The smallest unit of life; carries out the functions needed to live.
Parts inside a cell with specific jobs: nucleus, mitochondria, ribosomes, chloroplasts.
Cells adapted for a specific role, e.g. red blood cell, sperm, root hair.
A cell with a nucleus enclosed in a membrane; e.g. animal, plant, fungus cells.

mcqs.q: A bacterium is 2 µm long. How many fit end-to-end across a 1 mm gap?
options: 400 bacteria
750 bacteria
500 bacteria
250 bacteria

mcqs.q: A student places identical potato cylinders in a range of sugar solutions and records mass change. In strong sugar solution the cylinders lose mass. Which process explains this?
options: Osmosis — water left the cells by moving to lower water potential.
Active transport of sugar into the cells.
Diffusion of starch out of the cells.
Respiration using up the cell mass.

mcqs.q: Root hair cells take up mineral ions from soil even when the soil has a lower ion concentration than the cell. Which process is responsible?
options: Active transport, using energy from respiration
Diffusion down a concentration gradient
Osmosis of ions across the membrane
Evaporation through the root

mcqs.q: A drop of ink spreads out evenly in still water with no stirring. This is an example of:
options: Diffusion
Active transport
Osmosis
Phagocytosis

mcqs.q: Why do smaller cells exchange substances with their surroundings more efficiently than larger cells?
options: They have a larger surface area to volume ratio.
They have a smaller surface area to volume ratio.
They do not need to respire.
They contain no cytoplasm.
